newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 9.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Telephone: 11-3324842, 11-3761233; Fax: 91-11-3351006 Internet : biznis.news@forums.sprintrpg.sprint.com
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
RAIDS ON EX-CHIEF MINISTER'S HOUSE LEADS TO ARSON

Raids on the premises of former Tamil Nadu (TN) chief minister J. Jayalalitha continued in connection with her alleged role in the multi-million rupee colour television purchase scam even as her frenzied supporters indulged in arson in various parts of the state. The former TN chief minister is presently in jail following her arrest on Saturday. Jayalalitha's arrest saw her supporters take to the streets setting buses on fire, damaging 75 of them. The state government detained many of them to maintain peace.
The Times Of India
GOVERNMENT RAPPED FOR LAXITY ON DEFENCE ISSUES

H.D. Kumaraswamy, son of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, joined 40 members of the parliamentary standing committee on defence in rapping the government for its lack of concern on security issues. The 41-member committee includes the former lower house speaker and eight former cabinet ministers. Kumaraswamy flayed his father's government for having failed to activate the National Security Council.
Financial Express
FIXATION WITH DEFICIT DEPLORED

The mid-term appraisal report of the eighth five-year plan expressed serious reservations about the Finance Ministry's policy to reduce the budgetary deficit to 40 billion rupees by March 1997 and thereafter phasing out the ad-hoc treasury bills. The Planning Commission report also pulled up the government for excessive fiscal deficit which resulted in a severe expenditure compression in certain key sectors. It said the interest payments would continue to be the major claimant of the government's revenue receipts in the years to come, thereby constraining expenditure on infrastructure and the social sector.
BANKS TOLD TO SPEED UP SHARE PURCHASES

Commercial banks are under pressure from the Finance Ministry to purchase shares from the secondary market without further delay. Although the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), permitted the banks to pick up shares from the secondary market in its busy season monetary policy in October, none of the banks has yet taken the plunge. The ministry has also initiated a dialogue with the RBI to explore the possibility of lifting the cap on banks' investment in shares and debentures from the existing level of five percent of the incremental deposits of the previous year. The ministry's move is aimed at boosting the sagging market sentiment.
The Economic Times

A.P. MOLLER PLANS TO PARTICIPATE IN OIL, POWER SECTORS Danish industrial conglomerate A.P. Moller group plans to take up oil and natural gas exploration activities in India. The decision follows the opening up of the sector and an invitation by a reputed Indian business house. The group also plans to bid for big power projects in the country. About 15 years ago, the Danish group had initiated exploration work in Bombay High at the behest of the government, but had to wind up operations later following a ban on the entry of multinationals in the exploration sector. DABHOL POWER NOT TO GET 16 PCT GUARANTEED RETURN

Dhabol Power Company will not be given the 16 percent post-tax guaranteed return on the additional equity that it will bring in due to cost overruns, according to institutional lenders to the project. The cost overrun caused by delay is not being taken as part of the project cost as this would have upset the tariff that has been finalised. Therefore, the $160 million that the company will bring in over the original equity of $275 million will not be guaranteed a post-tax rate of return of 16 percent, the source said. The total cost of Phase I of the project was $920 million, $645 million being its debt component and $275 million its equity component.
NOD FOR MUTUAL FUNDS' BONUS, RIGHTS ISSUES LIKELY

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has convened a board meeting to discuss the depressed capital market. The board will also devise a policy framework on rights and bonus issues for mutual funds. Besides, the meeting will take up the issue of allowing the setting up of new stock exchanges. The meeting is being held against the backdrop of persistent demands from various sections that the government and SEBI announce a package to revive the capital market.
BOMBAY STOCK EXCHANGE FORWARD GROUP PLUNGES

The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) Forward or A Group, comprising 60 largely blue chip stocks, has lost 890.43 billion rupees in value, or 34 percent in market capitalisation, since April 30, 1996. The fall was even steeper than that witnessed in the non-specified groups of roughly 5,930 scrips, which lost 881.09 billion rupees, or 27 percent, in the same period. Total market capitalisation was down from 5,978.44 billion rupees on April 30 to 4,206.91 billion rupees as on December 2. The total loss in market capitalisation on BSE now stood at 1,771.53 billion rupees or 29.78 percent.
Business Standard
RETHINK ON FOREIGN INVESTMENT IN GOVERNMENT DEBT

The Finance Ministry is re-examining the possibility of permitting investment by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) in government debt. The ministry's move is aimed at reviving the domestic debt market. So far there have been no takers for the government's move to relax the rules and permit FII participation in corporate debt. The Finance Ministry last week invited Merrill Lynch to make a presentation on the measures to be taken to develop the domestic debt markets as a step towards reviving FII interest in funding infrastructure projects.
GLOBAL CONNECT ROAMING SERVICE IN 135 COUNTRIES

The Global Connect alliance of 16 cellular operators in the country proposes to offer international roaming in around 135 countries and has sought the central bank (RBI)'s permission to do so. The alliance was recently launched in Delhi. It allows subscribers with any one of the 16 services to send and receive calls throughout the country using the same SIM card. Diwaker Singh, Managing Director, Skycell Communications, an alliance member, said the Global Connect system would work differently from automatic roaming offered by the World One alliance announced by some other operators a few months ago.
The Observer
INDIA FIRM ON TELECOM OFFER

India is not going to improve its offer on the telecommunication services earlier given at Geneva, at the World Trade Organisation's (WTO) ministerial conference in Singapore. Sources said the Indian offer allowing 25 percent foreign participation in all telecommunication services would stand. Sources added India would watch what others would offer before reviewing its own offer, even though the United States had mentioned at the Geneva meeting of WTO that it was not happy with Indian offer.
